āpaṇa.notes: DPPN explicitly covers both DPD examples in one entry. SN 48.50 calls Āpaṇa a town of the Aṅgas. MN 54, MN 66, MN 92 and Snp 3.7 call it a town of the Aṅguttarāpans. The page references also pick up MN 53, MN 65, MN 91, MN 93 and SN 48.49, none of which names the town. Snp 3.7 is the Sela discourse cited in the entry but missing from its mapped citations. In that episode Sela and his students receive ordination and Keṇiya provides the meal. DPPN's claim that Keṇiya too was converted goes beyond the account.

ārāmadaṇḍa.notes: In the app's numbering, Mahākaccāna speaks with Ārāmadaṇḍa at Varaṇā in AN 2.37. DPD's AN 2.38 features Kandarāyana at Madhurā. DPPN gives sensual desire as the cause of both kinds of quarrel, but AN 2.37 distinguishes sensual desire among householders from attachment to views among ascetics. At the end Ārāmadaṇḍa takes refuge in Gotama, the teaching and the Saṅgha, asking Mahākaccāna to remember him as a lay follower.

ātumā.notes: The citation DN ii 131–2 has no mapped sutta in the packet. DN 16 at 4.30 names Ātumā twice as the Buddha tells Pukkusa about the threshing hut and the storm that killed two brothers and four oxen.

āṭānāṭā.notes: DN 32 lists Āṭānāṭā with Kusināṭā and Parakusināṭā among the cities built in the sky in the northern quarter.

īsāna.notes: DN 13 names Īsāna among the gods the brahmins invoke. In SN 11.3 Sakka tells the gods to look to Īsāna's banner if they cannot see Varuṇa's. The assurance about fear is Sakka's. The Buddha qualifies it at SN 11.3:7.1.
